finding.claim: Broken authorization on project deletion: `authorized()` returns a boolean but its result is discarded, so the ownership/admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can delete any project by ID. (Unlike `authorize()`, which throws.) A nonexistent ID also leaves `project` undefined and causes a TypeError, giving a 500 error.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/:id with another user's project id (req.params.id).

trace.note: DELETE /projects/:id handler, only requires req.user to exist
project loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) called; boolean return value ignored, no throw
authorized() only returns true/false, never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() call at line 18 is non-enforcing (return value unused). No other middleware visible in the repo (router is exported without auth middleware here; req.user is assumed to be set upstream). No ownership check in the store lookup. Compare PUT handler at line 25 which correctly uses the throwing authorize().

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:18 is a bare statement whose boolean result is discarded (defined at api.js:12-14, never throws); no other middleware or ownership filter exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the non-throwing boolean `authorized()` and ignores the result, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, unlike the throwing `authorize()` used at api.js:25.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: authorized() at api.js:12-14 only returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18; the throwing authorize() is used only in the PUT handler at api.js:25
verdict_facts.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:18 discards the boolean from authorized() (api.js:12-14), so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user; the PUT handler's throwing authorize() at api.js:25 confirms the intended check was missed.
